idea: Home-style tiffin delivery for hostel students in Bidholi, Dehradun

strategist.problem: Hostel students near UPES Bidholi at 8 PM realize the mess closed, Swiggy costs ₹250+, and no home-cooked option delivers to their gate tonight.
strategist.target_customer: Hostel-paying UPES students in Bidholi, Dehradun, spending ₹3,000-5,000 monthly on food, who skip or order junk when the mess underfeeds them.
strategist.mission: Deliver affordable, home-style tiffin meals daily to UPES hostel students in Bidholi who are tired of mess food and expensive delivery apps.

competitors.name: Local mess and dhaba tiffin services in Bidholi
competitors.differentiator: We win with a fixed monthly subscription, consistent home-style menu, and UPI payment links instead of daily cash negotiation.

competitors.name: Swiggy, Zomato and local restaurants delivering to Bidholi
competitors.differentiator: We win on price per meal and daily reliability for hostel students ordering 60+ meals a month.

competitors.name: Hostel mess food included in rent
competitors.differentiator: We win when the mess is closed, repetitive, or portion-light, which students feel at dinner time.

scope_cuts: No custom mobile app or website ordering system; WhatsApp and a Google Form handle orders until 50 paying subscribers.
No delivery fleet or hired delivery staff; founder or one helper delivers on a bicycle within a 2 km radius of Bidholi hostels.
No menu beyond 3 rotating daily options; a fixed rotating menu keeps kitchen prep simple for a student founder.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Free app handles daily orders, catalogue and quick replies for hostel students without building an app.

stack.name: Google Forms
stack.why: Free subscription sign-up form collects hostel, plan and UPI details before any payment.

stack.name: Google Sheets
stack.why: Free tracker logs subscribers, delivery days, UPI payments and kitchen prep counts.

stack.name: Razorpay
stack.why: Payment links collect monthly subscription via UPI at 2% + GST per transaction.

stack.name: Google Sites
stack.why: Free one-page menu and price list linkable in WhatsApp status and Instagram bio.

stack.name: Instagram
stack.why: Free business account posts reels of daily tiffin boxes to reach UPES students in Bidholi.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Writes the 30-day rotating menu, WhatsApp reply templates, Google Form questions and Instagram captions.

ai_tools.name: ChatGPT
ai_tools.why: Generates weekly grocery shopping lists and per-meal cost breakdowns from recipes.

ai_tools.name: Canva
ai_tools.why: Free plan designs the menu poster, UPI QR standee and Instagram post templates.

mvp_features: Monthly subscription: 30 dinners, one home-style tiffin per night, delivered to hostel gate by 8 PM within 2 km of Bidholi, paid via Razorpay UPI link.
Trial pack: 3 dinners at a one-time price, paid by UPI link, delivered the same week to convert mess-tired students.
Menu: 3 rotating dinner options (dal-chawal-sabzi, rajma-chawal, kadhi-chawal) with fixed weekly rotation, one roti batch per option.

tool_costs.price_note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

first_10_steps: Message 10 UPES hostel students in Bidholi WhatsApp groups asking what they'd pay monthly for a home-style dinner tiffin.
List 3 dinner options with ChatGPT and price each meal's raw ingredients from a Bidholi kirana store quote.
Cook the 3 dinner options at home once, photograph each tiffin box, and note actual per-meal ingredient cost.
Build a Google Form with plan choice, hostel name, room number and UPI ID; link it in a Google Sites one-page menu.
Create the menu poster in Canva free and post it to Instagram and 5 hostel WhatsApp groups.
Open a Razorpay account and generate 1 payment link per plan; test a ₹1 UPI payment yourself.
Take 5 pre-orders via the Google Form and Razorpay link before buying any bulk groceries.
Buy groceries for the first 5 subscribers' 3-day deliveries from a Bidholi kirana store using the pre-order money.
Deliver the first tiffins by bicycle within 2 km of Bidholi hostels before 8 PM and collect WhatsApp feedback.
Post a Canva testimonial reel from the first 5 subscribers and open the monthly subscription link to the full hostel list.

pricing.name: Trial Pack (3 dinners)
features: 3 home-style dinners delivered to hostel gate within 2 km of Bidholi

pricing.name: Monthly Dinner Tiffin
features: 30 dinners delivered to hostel gate by 8 PM, rotating dal-chawal-sabzi, rajma-chawal, kadhi-chawal menu

pricing.name: Monthly Tiffin (Student Referral)
features: 30 dinners at ₹70/meal when a referred friend subscribes; same menu and delivery

burn_line_items.item: Marketing budget (Instagram feed promotion, printed A4 posters, gate sampling boxes)

revenue_targets.notes: 5 monthly subscribers from Bidholi hostel WhatsApp groups; founder cooks all meals personally, no paid cook in burn.
12 subscribers across 3-4 hostels; founder still cooks, one friend helps evening bicycle delivery unpaid.
25 subscribers; ₹15/meal cook labor (₹450/customer) is inside delivery_cost_per_customer of ₹1140, funded from revenue not burn.

key_assumptions: Students near UPES Bidholi pay ₹2400/month (₹80/dinner) for home-style tiffin vs ₹250+ Swiggy orders, based on a ₹3,000-₹5,000 monthly food budget.
delivery_cost_per_customer = ₹1140: ₹600 ingredients (₹20×30 dinners) + ₹450 cook labor (₹15×30 dinners, paid from revenue once founder outsources prep) + ₹90 packaging/bicycle share.
Founder cooks all meals personally until Day 90 revenue funds the ₹15/meal cook; cook cost sits in unit economics, not monthly burn.
Razorpay 2% + GST fees absorbed in delivery_cost_per_customer, not burn, since they scale with revenue.

channels.name: Hostel WhatsApp groups + gate sampling in Bidholi
channels.tactic: Post menu poster + ₹300 trial-pack Razorpay link in 8 UPES hostel WhatsApp groups and class groups, 2 posts/week each; hand 10 free sample boxes at hostel gates 6-8 PM, 3 days/week.

channels.name: Instagram reels + WhatsApp status of daily tiffin boxes
channels.tactic: Post 1 reel/day of the packed tiffin box at 7 PM on Instagram with Bidholi/UPES hashtags; repost to WhatsApp status daily; ₹600 Instagram feed promotion on 4 posts/month.

first_10_customers: Ask 3 batchmates in Bidholi hostels to forward your Google Form link into their hostel WhatsApp groups on Day 1.
DM 20 UPES students from your class contact list personally with the cold message and trial-pack link.
Stand at the hostel gate 6-8 PM for 3 days and hand 10 free sample boxes to students you meet, asking for ₹300 trial sign-up if they liked it.
Offer the first 5 subscribers a referral: ₹300 off next month when their friend subscribes, tracked in Google Sheets.
Post the same trial offer in 2 UPES college club WhatsApp groups (hostel rep and fest committees) on Day 4 and Day 11.
Call 5 students who filled the Google Form but didn't pay, and ask what stopped them.
growth.cold_message:
Hi, I'm a UPES student starting a home-style dinner tiffin delivered to your hostel gate by 8 PM — dal-chawal, rajma-chawal, kadhi-chawal rotation, ₹80/dinner, ₹2400/month.
Swiggy dinner costs ₹250+; mine is ₹80 and reaches your gate.
Want a 3-dinner trial for ₹300 this week? I'll send the UPI link — no commitment.

objections.objection: Mess food is already included in my hostel rent, why pay extra?
objections.response: This is for nights the mess closes early or repeats the same menu — take the ₹300 3-dinner trial first, and only subscribe if you actually eat it.
Start with the ₹300 trial pack of 3 dinners, or refer a friend and both pay ₹2100/month instead of ₹2400.

critic.verdict: The plan is a coherent, low-cost physical tiffin service for UPES hostel students with a realistic free-tool stack and a campus-first launch that fits a student founder's 15 hours a week. Pricing at ₹2400/month for 30 dinners is plausible against Swiggy but tight on margin once real ingredient inflation and delivery time are counted, and the day-30 target of 5 paying customers in 30 days is ambitious for a first-time food vendor with no food-safety or FSSAI setup mentioned. Overall it's executable within the ₹15,000 cap, but a few gaps around food compliance and delivery-cost realism need attention.
critic.biggest_risk: Selling ₹2400/month home-cooked dinners as an unknown student with no FSSAI registration or food-safety proof — students and hostels may balk at trust/hygiene, and a single food-safety complaint could shut the operation down.
